questions.q: Convex mirrors are used in
questions.ans: B
sol: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wider field of view, so it is used as a rear view mirror.

questions.q: The sun is visible to us about two minutes before the actual sunrise and about two minutes even after the actual sunset because of atmospheric
questions.ans: A
sol: Light from the sun bends (refracts) as it passes through layers of air of different density, so we see the sun a little before it rises and after it sets.

questions.q: A current carrying rod is placed between the poles of a horse-shoe magnet. For the maximum displacement of the rod the angle between the direction of electric current and the direction of magnetic field must be
questions.ans: C
sol: The force on a current-carrying conductor is greatest when the current is perpendicular (90°) to the magnetic field.

questions.q: Draw a symbol diagram of a resistor used in an electric circuit.
questions.ans: A zig-zag line (or a small rectangle) between two straight wire ends
sol: Draw a short straight wire, then a zig-zag line, then a short straight wire: —╱╲╱╲—. (A small rectangle in a straight line is also accepted.)

questions.q: “Two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other.” Justify.
questions.ans: At a crossing point a compass would point in two directions at once, which is impossible.
sol: The tangent to a field line gives the direction of the field. If two lines crossed, the field would have two directions at that point, so a compass needle would point two ways at once. This is not possible, so field lines never intersect.

questions.q: Observe the circuit diagram given below. Mention the direction of magnetic field that forms around the point P and around the point Q.
questions.fig: A circular loop connected to a cell. Current goes up the left side of the loop through point P, across the top, and down the right side through point Q. Concentric field circles are drawn around P and Q.
questions.ans: Around P: anticlockwise. Around Q: clockwise.
sol: Use the right-hand thumb rule. Current flows in opposite directions at P and Q (up through P, down through Q).
So the field lines around P and Q go in opposite directions: anticlockwise around P and clockwise around Q.

questions.q: Explain Newton’s experiment that shows the recombination of spectrum of white light.
questions.ans: A second, inverted identical prism recombines the spectrum into white light.
sol: Newton passed white light through a glass prism, which split it into a spectrum of seven colours.
He placed a second identical prism upside down (inverted) next to the first.
All the colours passed through the second prism and came out as white light.
This shows white light is made of seven colours, which recombine to give white light.

questions.q: Write any two differences between near-sighted (Myopic) and far-sighted (Hypermetropic) eyes.
questions.ans: Myopia: sees near, image in front of retina, concave lens. Hypermetropia: sees far, image behind retina, convex lens.
sol: Myopia: near objects are clear but distant objects are blurred. Hypermetropia: distant objects are clear but near objects are blurred.
Myopia: image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. Hypermetropia: image of a near object forms behind the retina.
Myopia is corrected with a concave lens; hypermetropia with a convex lens.
Causes: myopia – eyeball too long or lens too curved; hypermetropia – eyeball too short or focal length too long.

questions.q: Draw the ray diagram of image formed when an object is kept at 2F₁ of the convex lens. With the help of the ray diagram write the position and nature of the image. (F₁: Principal focus of the lens)
questions.ans: Image at 2F₂; real, inverted, same size as the object
sol: Draw the principal axis with the convex lens at O. Mark F₁, 2F₁ on the left and F₂, 2F₂ on the right.
Place the object AB at 2F₁.
Ray 1: from A parallel to the axis, refracting through F₂.
Ray 2: from A through the optical centre O, going straight.
The rays meet at 2F₂ below the axis, giving image A′B′.
Position: at 2F₂. Nature: real, inverted and the same size as the object.

questions.q: a) State Ohm’s law. b) Write the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.
questions.ans: V = IR at constant temperature; R depends on length, area of cross-section, material and temperature.
sol: a) At constant temperature, the current through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends: V ∝ I, or V = IR.

b) Resistance depends on: (i) length – R increases with length (R ∝ l); (ii) area of cross-section – R decreases as area increases (R ∝ 1/A); (iii) nature of the material (resistivity); (iv) temperature.

questions.q: a) What factor helps for determining the relative strength of a magnetic field? b) What is solenoid? How is an electromagnet prepared by using it?
questions.ans: Closeness of field lines; a solenoid is a closely wound cylindrical coil; put a soft iron core inside and pass current.
sol: a) The degree of closeness of the field lines: where the lines are crowded, the field is stronger.
b) A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.
To make an electromagnet, place a soft iron rod (core) inside the solenoid and pass an electric current. The strong field inside magnetises the iron.

or.q: In domestic electric circuits, a) What is the function of earth wire? b) What precautions should be taken to avoid overloading?
or.ans: Earth wire gives leakage current a low-resistance path to earth; avoid many appliances on one socket and use fuses/MCBs.
sol: a) The earth wire connects the metal body of an appliance to the earth. It gives any leakage current a low-resistance path to the ground, keeping the body at earth potential so the user does not get a severe shock.

b) Do not connect too many appliances to a single socket; do not use high-power appliances at the same time on one line; use a fuse or MCB of the correct rating; avoid damaged insulation that can cause short circuits.

questions.q: a) How is an ammeter and a voltmeter connected to an electric circuit? Mention their function. b) “In domestic electric circuit, the electrical appliances are generally connected in parallel.” Give reasons.
questions.ans: Ammeter in series (measures current); voltmeter in parallel (measures potential difference).
sol: a) An ammeter is connected in series; it measures the electric current in the circuit.
A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component; it measures the potential difference across it.
b) In parallel, each appliance gets the full mains voltage.
Each appliance can be switched on or off independently, and if one fails the others keep working.
Each appliance draws the current it needs because the total resistance is lower.

questions.q: The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 36 cm. Find its focal length. A candle of 5 cm length is placed at a distance of 27 cm in front of a convex mirror of the same focal length. Mention the position and nature of the image and also find the size of the image formed.
questions.ans: f = 18 cm; image 10.8 cm behind the mirror, virtual, erect, 2 cm tall
sol: f = R/2 = 36/2 = 18 cm. For a convex mirror f = +18 cm; u = −27 cm; h = 5 cm.
The image is 10.8 cm behind the mirror.
Nature: virtual, erect and diminished.

or.q: The focal length of a spherical mirror is 10 cm. Find its radius of curvature. An object of 4 cm size is placed at 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of the same focal length. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed in order to obtain a sharp image of the object? Mention the nature of the image formed and also find the size of the image.
or.ans: R = 20 cm; screen 20 cm in front of the mirror; real, inverted, 4 cm (same size)
sol: R = 2f = 20 cm.
Concave mirror: f = −10 cm, u = −20 cm, h = 4 cm.
Place the screen 20 cm in front of the mirror (at C).
Nature: real, inverted and the same size as the object.

questions.q: Correct statement related to the soaps among the following is, soaps
opts: easily give excess of foam in hard water
form insoluble precipitate in hard water
easily clean oils like dirt in hard water
are sodium salts of sulphonic acid
questions.ans: B
sol: Soaps react with calcium and magnesium salts in hard water to form an insoluble precipitate called scum.

questions.q: CuO + H₂ →(heat) Cu + H₂O. In this chemical reaction,
opts: hydrogen is reduced to form water
exchange of ions took place between the reactants
copper oxide is oxidised to form copper
copper oxide is reduced to form copper
questions.ans: D
sol: Copper oxide loses oxygen to become copper, so it is reduced. (Hydrogen gains oxygen and is oxidised.)

questions.q: Mention any two measures for preventing corrosion of iron.
questions.ans: Painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising, chrome plating, making alloys
sol: Any two: painting, oiling or greasing, galvanising (coating with zinc), chrome plating, anodising, or making alloys such as stainless steel.

questions.q: How is concentrated acid diluted?
questions.ans: Add the acid slowly to water with constant stirring.
sol: The acid must be added slowly to water with constant stirring, never water to acid, because the process is highly exothermic and the mixture can splash.

questions.q: What is rancidity? Mention any two methods of preventing rancidity.
questions.ans: Oxidation of fats/oils that spoils smell and taste; prevent with antioxidants, airtight containers or nitrogen packing.
sol: Rancidity: when fats and oils in food are oxidised, their smell and taste change. This is called rancidity.
Prevention (any two): add antioxidants; store food in airtight containers; flush packets with nitrogen gas; keep food in a refrigerator.

questions.q: Give reason: a) Zinc oxide is called as an amphoteric oxide b) Sodium metal is stored in kerosene.
questions.ans: ZnO reacts with both acids and bases; sodium reacts vigorously with air and water.
sol: a) Zinc oxide reacts with both acids and bases to give salt and water: ZnO + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂O; ZnO + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂O. So it is amphoteric.
b) Sodium reacts so vigorously with oxygen and moisture that it catches fire in open air. Keeping it in kerosene prevents contact with air and water.

or.q: Give reason: a) Gold is used to make jewellery b) Ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity.
or.ans: Gold is lustrous, malleable and does not tarnish; ions in a solid cannot move.
sol: a) Gold is lustrous, highly malleable and ductile, and does not corrode or tarnish in air, so it keeps its shine.
b) In the solid state the ions are held in fixed positions by strong forces and cannot move, so no current flows. They conduct when molten or dissolved.

questions.q:
Complete the following oxidation reaction and name the functional group that is found in the product:
CH₃CH₂OH → (alkaline [ ] + heat, or acidified [ ] + heat) → [ ]
questions.ans: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH using alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇; functional group: carboxylic acid (–COOH)
sol: Oxidising agents: alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) or acidified potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇), with heat.
CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH (ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid).
The functional group in the product is the carboxylic acid group, –COOH.

questions.q: Draw the diagram of the arrangement of apparatus used to show the electrolytic refining of copper. Label the following parts: i) Cathode ii) Impurities.
questions.ans: Diagram
sol: Draw a tank filled with acidified copper sulphate solution (the electrolyte).
Hang a thick block of impure copper as the anode, connected to the positive terminal of a battery.
Hang a thin strip of pure copper as the cathode, connected to the negative terminal. Label it ‘Cathode’.
Show a deposit of insoluble impurities (anode mud) at the bottom below the anode. Label it ‘Impurities’.

questions.q: Write the chemical equations for the following reactions. i) Quicklime is reacted with water ii) Zinc pieces are added to copper sulphate solution iii) Sodium chloride solution is added to silver nitrate solution.
questions.ans: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂; Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu; NaCl + AgNO₃ → AgCl + NaNO₃
sol: i) CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂
ii) Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
iii) NaCl + AgNO₃ → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃

or.q: Balance the following chemical equations: i) H₂ + O₂ → H₂O ii) Na₂CO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ iii) N₂ + H₂ → NH₃
sol: i) 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
ii) Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂
iii) N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃

questions.q: a) NaOH, Ca(OH)₂, H₂ and Cl₂ materials are given to you. By using which of these materials, you can prepare bleaching powder? Write the chemical name and one use of the bleaching powder. b) i) How do you identify a solution as basic solution by using blue litmus paper? ii) Under what condition does a farmer treat the soil of his field with slaked lime?
questions.ans: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂; calcium oxychloride; turn blue litmus red with acid first; when soil is acidic.
sol: a) Use Ca(OH)₂ (dry slaked lime) and Cl₂: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.
Chemical name: calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂).
Uses (any one): bleaching cotton and linen; disinfecting drinking water; as an oxidising agent.
b) i) A base does not change blue litmus. So first dip the blue litmus in an acid to turn it red, then dip it in the solution. If it turns blue again, the solution is basic.
ii) When the soil of the field is too acidic.

questions.q: a) Write any two differences between saturated and unsaturated carbon compounds. b) What are structural isomers? Write the structural isomers of butane. c) Write the electron dot structure of methane molecule.
questions.ans: Single vs double/triple bonds; same formula, different structures; n-butane and isobutane; C shares one pair with each H.
sol: a) Saturated compounds have only single bonds between carbon atoms; unsaturated compounds have double or triple bonds.
Saturated compounds are less reactive and burn with a clean blue flame; unsaturated compounds are more reactive, undergo addition reactions and burn with a sooty yellow flame.
b) Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called structural isomers.
Butane (C₄H₁₀): n-butane CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ and isobutane (2-methylpropane) CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃.
c) Methane (CH₄): carbon in the centre with 4 valence electrons shares one pair of electrons with each of four hydrogen atoms (4 single covalent bonds), so every H has 2 electrons and C has 8.

questions.q: The information source for making proteins in the cells is
questions.ans: C
sol: Cellular DNA is the information source for making proteins in the cell. A section of DNA that carries the information for one protein is the gene for that protein.

questions.q: Blood sugar level increases : Undersecretion of insulin hormone :: Swelling of the neck : ..................
questions.ans: A
sol: A swollen neck (goitre) is caused by too little thyroxine, usually from lack of iodine in the diet.

questions.q: Type of asexual reproduction that occurs in spirogyra is
questions.ans: D
sol: Spirogyra simply breaks into smaller pieces when mature, and each piece grows into a new individual. This is fragmentation.

questions.q: What is the function of ozone layer?
questions.ans: It absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
sol: The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun and protects living things on earth from it.

questions.q: What is neuron?
questions.ans: A nerve cell: the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.
sol: A neuron is a nerve cell, the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

questions.q: The events that occur during photosynthesis are given below. Write these events in correct order. i) Splitting of water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen ii) Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll iii) Conversion of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates iv) Conversion of light energy to chemical energy.
questions.ans: ii → iv → i → iii
sol: Absorption of light by chlorophyll (ii) → conversion of light energy to chemical energy (iv) → splitting of water (i) → reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates (iii).

questions.q: How do auxins promote the growth of tendrils of climbing plants around a support?
questions.ans: Auxin moves away from the contact side, so the far side grows faster and the tendril coils round the support.
sol: When a tendril touches a support, the part in contact grows less than the part away from it.
Auxin collects on the side away from the support and makes the cells there grow longer.
The faster growth on the outer side makes the tendril coil around the support.

or.q: How does our body respond when adrenaline is secreted into the blood?
or.ans: Faster heartbeat and breathing, more blood to muscles; the body prepares for emergency.
sol: The heart beats faster, supplying more oxygen to the muscles.
Blood supply to the digestive system and skin is reduced (small arteries there contract) and diverted to skeletal muscles.
Breathing rate increases as the diaphragm and rib muscles contract.
Together these prepare the body to deal with an emergency (fight or flight).

questions.q: Construct a food chain using the organisms; snake, frog, grass and grasshopper. Which organism has more accumulation of harmful chemicals in this food chain?
questions.ans: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake; the snake
sol: Food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake.
The snake, at the highest trophic level, has the most harmful chemicals because they increase at each level (biological magnification).

questions.q: Draw the diagram showing the germination of pollen on stigma and label ‘ovary’.
questions.ans: Diagram
sol: Draw the pistil: stigma at the top, a long style, and a swollen ovary at the base containing an ovule (with the female germ cell).
Show pollen grains on the stigma, with one pollen tube growing down through the style to the ovule.
Label the swollen base ‘Ovary’.

questions.q: What is the role of the following enzymes in human alimentary canal? i) Trypsin ii) Amylase iii) Lipase
questions.ans: Trypsin digests proteins; amylase turns starch into sugar; lipase breaks fats into fatty acids and glycerol.
sol: i) Trypsin (from the pancreas) digests proteins.
ii) Salivary amylase breaks down starch into simple sugar (maltose).
iii) Lipase breaks down emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: Justify the following statements: a) Sexual type of reproduction leads to more variations. b) In woman’s uterus the role of placenta is significant for the development of foetus.
questions.ans: DNA from two parents combines; the placenta passes food and oxygen to the embryo and removes wastes.
sol: a) In sexual reproduction, germ cells from two individuals combine, so DNA from two parents mixes in new combinations. This produces more variation.
b) The placenta is a disc embedded in the uterine wall with villi on the embryo’s side, giving a large surface area.
Glucose and oxygen pass from the mother’s blood to the embryo through it, and wastes from the embryo pass to the mother’s blood.

or.q: a) How does menstruation occur in women? b) In male reproductive system the testes are located outside the abdominal cavity in scrotum. Why?
or.ans: Unused uterine lining breaks down and is shed; sperm form at a lower temperature than body temperature.
sol: a) Each month the uterus prepares a thick, spongy lining to receive a fertilised egg. If the egg is not fertilised, this lining is not needed. It breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus. This is menstruation, and it lasts about 2 to 8 days.
b) Sperm formation needs a temperature lower than the normal body temperature, so the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum.

questions.q: Draw the diagram showing the structure of human brain. Label the following parts: i) Hypothalamus ii) Medulla
questions.ans: Diagram
sol: Draw a side view of the brain: the large folded cerebrum on top, the cerebellum at the back below it, and the brain stem going down to the spinal cord.
Label ‘Hypothalamus’ at the base of the forebrain, just below the centre of the cerebrum.
Label ‘Medulla’ at the lowest part of the brain stem, joining the spinal cord.

questions.q: Round green colour (RRyy) seeds producing pea plant is crossed with wrinkled yellow colour (rrYY) seeds producing pea plant. Show the result of F₂ generation with the help of a checker board and write the ratio of varieties of plants.
questions.ans: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green
sol: Parents RRyy × rrYY. F₁: all RrYy (round, yellow).
F₁ gametes: RY, Ry, rY, ry. Make a 4 × 4 checker board with these on both sides.
Count the 16 boxes: round yellow (R_Y_) = 9, round green (R_yy) = 3, wrinkled yellow (rrY_) = 3, wrinkled green (rryy) = 1.

or.q: a) Explain the sex determination of a child in human beings. b) How can the traits of organisms be decided as either dominant or recessive?
or.ans: The father’s sperm (X or Y) decides the sex; the trait seen in F₁ is dominant.
sol: a) Women have XX sex chromosomes; men have XY.
All eggs carry an X. Half the sperms carry X and half carry Y.
An X sperm fertilising the egg gives XX (a girl); a Y sperm gives XY (a boy). So the sex of the child is decided by the father’s sperm.

b) Cross two pure-breeding plants with contrasting traits. The trait that appears in the F₁ generation is dominant. The trait that is hidden in F₁ and reappears in about one-fourth of the F₂ plants is recessive.

questions.q: a) Explain briefly the role of haemoglobin pigments present in our blood. b) What are the different strategies of excretion found in plants?
questions.ans: Haemoglobin carries oxygen to tissues; plants excrete through stomata, transpiration, falling leaves, vacuoles, gums/resins and the soil.
sol: a) Haemoglobin is a respiratory pigment in red blood cells with a high affinity for oxygen. It takes up oxygen in the lungs and carries it to tissues that need it.
b) Plants remove oxygen and carbon dioxide through stomata, and excess water by transpiration.
Wastes are stored in leaves that fall off, or in cell vacuoles.
Some wastes are stored as resins and gums in old xylem.
Some wastes are released into the soil around the roots.
